# Module Reference

Every module RoleCall can dispatch in a task — either in Ansible-style collapsed form (`copy: { dest }`) or explicitly (`module: copy` with `args:`). Listed programmatically from the runtime `meta` (mirrors `rolecall docs modules`).

## acl

Set or remove a filesystem ACL entry (Ansible `acl` alternate). Wraps `setfacl`/`getfacl`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Target file/dir. |
| `entity` | `string` | required | User or group name. |
| `etype` | `user \| group` | optional | Entity type (default user). |
| `permissions` | `string` | required | ACL permissions, e.g. rwx. |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | present (default). |
| `default` | `boolean` | optional | Set a default ACL. |
| `recursive` | `boolean` | optional | Apply the ACL recursively (-R) to the path. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- acl:
    path: /srv/shared
    entity: deploy
    etype: user
    permissions: rwx
```


> ≠ Ansible `acl`: no `follow`/mask recalculation toggles; single entry per task (recursive applies -R to that entry).

## add_host

Add a host (and groups) to the in-memory inventory at runtime (Ansible `add_host` alternate). The spec is returned in `data.add_host`; capture with `register:`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Hostname to add. |
| `groups` | `string` | optional | Comma-separated groups. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- add_host:
    name: "{{ item }}"
    groups: webservers
  loop:
    $each:
      $var: vars.new_hosts
```


> Registers the host into the run-level dynamic inventory (`ExecOptions.dynamicHosts`) and into the resolved host set so subsequent `hosts: all` tasks target it within the same run; the spec is also returned in `data.add_host` for `register:`. For SSH transports the host's connection vars (ansible_host, etc.) must be supplied so the transport can connect.

## apt_repository

Manage an APT source line (Ansible `apt_repository` alternate) under /etc/apt/sources.list.d. Idempotent: re-running with the same repo is a no-op and other lines in the file are preserved.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | `string` | required | Full apt source line, e.g. 'deb http://archive.ubuntu.com/ubuntu jammy main'. |
| `filename` | `string` | optional | File under sources.list.d (default rolecall.list); '.list' is appended when missing. |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |
| `validate_certs` | `boolean` | optional | Validate the repository TLS certificate (default true). When false, the source line gets an apt [trusted=yes] option. |
| `update_cache` | `boolean` | optional | Run `apt-get update` after the source list changes (default false). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- apt_repository:
    repo: "deb http://apt.nginx.org/ubuntu jammy nginx"
    filename: nginx.list
    state: present
```

```yaml
- apt_repository:
    repo: "deb [arch=amd64] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu jammy stable"
    filename: docker.list
    update_cache: true
```


> ≠ Ansible `apt_repository`: `filename` defaults to rolecall.list (not a URL-derived name), `update_cache` defaults to false, and `codename`/`arch`/`signed_by`/`comment` are not auto-composed — pass a complete `repo` line instead. `validate_certs: false` maps to an apt `[trusted=yes]` source option. Uses `$var` refs, not Jinja `{{ }}`.

## archive

Bundle files on the target into an archive (Ansible `archive` alternate). Supports tar/zip; always recreates the archive (not diff-based).

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Destination archive path. |
| `src` | `string \| string[]` | required | Files/dirs to include. |
| `format` | `tar \| zip` | optional | Archive format (default tar; zip if path ends .zip). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- archive:
    path: /backup/etc.tar
    src:
      - /etc/nginx
      - /etc/ssh
```


> ≠ Ansible `archive`: always recreates the archive (no `remove`/mtime check); no `exclude_path` filtering yet.

## assemble

Concatenate files from a remote directory into one file (Ansible `assemble` alternate). Reads each matching file on the target and writes the concatenation to `dest`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | required | Remote directory to read parts from. |
| `dest` | `string` | required | Remote destination file. |
| `regexp` | `string` | optional | Only include filenames matching this regex. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- assemble:
    src: /etc/nginx/conf.d
    dest: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf.assembled
    regexp: '.*.conf$'
```


> ≠ Ansible `assemble`: `remote_src` is always true (RoleCall reads from the target); files are concatenated in sorted filename order. No `delimiter` insertion between parts yet.

## assert

Fails (failed:true) when the `that` condition is falsy; guards control flow and tests failure paths.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `that` | `unknown` | optional | Condition that must be truthy for the assertion to pass. |
| `msg` | `string` | optional | Failure message when `that` is falsy. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- assert:
    that:
      $and:
        - $var: vars.ok
        - $eq:
          - $var: vars.env
          - 'prod'
    msg: 'require ok flag and prod environment'
```

```yaml
- assert:
    that:
      $not:
        $in:
          - $var: vars.cfg_file
          - $var: vars.available_files
    msg: 'configuration file must be supplied'
```

```yaml
- assert:
    that:
      $or:
        - $eq:
          - $var: vars.mode
          - 'dry'
        - $gt:
          - $var: vars.retry_count
          - 0
    msg: 'proceed when dry-run or retries remain'
```


> ≠ Ansible `assert`: conditions use RoleCall's structured `$var`/`$eq`/`$gt`/`$and` expression ops (rendered like any other arg), not Jinja `when`. `that` is truthy-tested; `msg` is the failure text.

## authorized_key

Manage an SSH authorized_keys entry (Ansible `authorized_key` alternate). Adds/removes the `key` line for `user` idempotently; creates the file with 0600 if missing.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `user` | `string` | optional | Target user (default root). |
| `key` | `string` | required | Public key line (e.g. 'ssh-rsa AAAA...'). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |
| `exclusive` | `boolean` | optional | Replace all other keys with this one. |
| `path` | `string` | optional | Explicit authorized_keys path. |
| `comment` | `string` | optional | Trailing comment appended to the key line (e.g. an owner note). |
| `key_options` | `string` | optional | Options prefix before the key, e.g. 'command="..."' or 'no-port-forwarding'. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- authorized_key:
    user: deploy
    key: "ssh-rsa AAAA... user@laptop"
    exclusive: true
```


> ≠ Ansible `authorized_key`: `manage_dir` not modeled (the dir is always created with 0600); matches keys by type+base64. `comment`/`key_options` are supported on the written line.

## blockinfile

Idempotent block-in-file module: inserts/replaces/removes a marker-delimited block only when needed. Supports optional backup and a validate command run on the file after writing.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Destination path on the target. |
| `block` | `string` | required | Block body to insert/ensure (multiline allowed). |
| `marker` | `string` | optional | Marker template; {mark} becomes BEGIN &lt;id&gt; / END &lt;id&gt;. Default '# RoleCall BLOCK {mark}'. |
| `marker_id` | `string` | optional | Id used inside the markers. Default 'block'. |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |
| `insertafter` | `EOF \| START` | optional | Where to insert when absent (default EOF). |
| `backup` | `boolean` | optional | Back up the existing file (a timestamped `.bak` sibling, attributes preserved) before writing. Defaults to false. |
| `validate` | `string` | optional | Validation command run against the file after writing; `%s` is replaced with the file path. The task fails if the command exits non-zero (e.g. `nginx -t -c %s`). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- blockinfile:
    path: /etc/hosts
    block: |
      10.0.0.1 host1
      10.0.0.2 host2
    state: present
```

```yaml
- blockinfile:
  loop:
    $each:
      $var: play.hosts
    path: /etc/hosts
    marker_id:
      $var: loop.item
    block:
      $concat:
        - 'host-'
        - $var: loop.item
    state: present
```


> ≠ Ansible `blockinfile`: the marker default is `# RoleCall BLOCK {mark}` (not `# BEGIN/END ANSIBLE MANAGED BLOCK`). Uses `$var` refs, not Jinja `{{ }}`.

## command

Ansible `command`/`raw` alias of `shell`. Forwards to `shell` with `run_mode: always` (changed every run) or `run_mode: idempotent` when a `creates`/`removes` guard is set (or an explicit `run_mode`). RoleCall always executes via /bin/sh.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cmd` | `string` | required | Command to run (alias: command). |
| `command` | `string` | optional | Alias for `cmd`. |
| `creates` | `string` | optional | Skip when this path exists (maps to shell idempotent guard). |
| `removes` | `string` | optional | Skip when this path is absent (maps to shell idempotent guard). |
| `chdir` | `string` | optional | Directory to cd into first (translated to a `cd` prefix). |
| `run_mode` | `idempotent \| readonly \| always` | optional | Override the forwarded shell run_mode (default: always, or idempotent when a guard is set). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- command:
    cmd: /usr/sbin/setup-balancers.py
    creates: /etc/balancers-enabled
```

```yaml
- command:
    cmd: /opt/app/run.sh
    chdir: /opt/app
    creates: /opt/app/.bootstrapped
```


> ≠ Ansible `command`/`raw`: `command` is an alias of `shell` (no separate no-shell path). A path guard (`creates`/`removes`) makes it `run_mode: idempotent` (skips when satisfied); otherwise it is `run_mode: always` (changed every run). `raw` is the same alias — RoleCall's transport is already shell-based, so there is no Python-less special case. Guards are NOT allowed with `run_mode: readonly`/`always` on `shell`; `command` picks `idempotent` for you when a guard is present, or set `run_mode` explicitly.

## config_edit

Idempotent structured/file editor: merges/replaces a json/yaml/ini key (or a fenced xml/text block) only when the current state differs.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Destination path on the target. |
| `format` | `json \| yaml \| ini \| xml \| text` | optional | Structured format for key merge (json/yaml/ini) or fenced block mode (xml/text). |
| `key` | `string` | optional | Dotted key path into the structure (structured modes). |
| `value` | `unknown` | optional | Desired value at key (structured present) or full value (no key). Note: value REPLACES the key — no native list-append. |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |
| `block` | `string` | optional | Fenced-block body for xml/text modes. |
| `marker` | `string` | optional | Marker template; {mark} becomes BEGIN/END + marker_id. |
| `marker_id` | `string` | optional | Id used inside the fenced markers. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- config_edit:
    path: /etc/app.json
    format: json
    key: port
    value: 8080
```


> `value` REPLACES the key (there is no native list-append this pass). Uses RoleCall's structured `$var`/`$concat`/`$call` refs, not Jinja `{{ }}`. Supersedes the removed `file` module for in-place edits.

## copy

Literal idempotent file copy to a remote target, or on-host template render (_content/template_file, EJS or Jinja). SHA-256 compare; ships bytes base64-encoded and decodes on-target in one compare+write script with atomic mv. Supports inline content, a local source file, optional mode/owner/group, backup, validate, become, and --check.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | optional | Local path to the source file on the control node. At least one of `src` or `content` is required. |
| `content` | `string \| { template, template_file, engine }` | optional | Inline content for the destination. A bare string is written verbatim (never interpreted as a template). Pass an object with `template` (inline string) or `template_file` (path) and optional `engine` ('ejs' default, or 'jinja') to render on-host. |
| `dest` | `string` | optional | Destination path on the target. |
| `path` | `string` | optional | Alias for `dest` (accepted for drop-in `config_write` parity). |
| `mode` | `string` | optional | Octal mode to apply after writing, e.g. '0644'. |
| `force` | `boolean` | optional | Rewrite unconditionally even when the destination already matches. Defaults to false (rewrite only on mismatch). |
| `backup` | `boolean` | optional | Back up an existing destination before overwriting it (a timestamped .bak sibling is created). Defaults to false. |
| `validate` | `string` | optional | Validation command run against the temp file before it is moved into place; `%s` is replaced with the temp path. The task fails if the command exits non-zero (e.g. `visudo -cf %s`). |
| `owner` | `string` | optional | Owner user to chown after writing. |
| `group` | `string` | optional | Group to chgrp after writing. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- copy:
    src: files/app.conf
    dest: /etc/app/app.conf
    mode: '0644'
```

```yaml
- copy:
    content: 'port=8080'
    dest: /etc/app/port.conf
```

```yaml
- copy:
    dest: /etc/nginx/conf.d/site.conf
    content:
      template_file: vhost.j2
      engine: jinja
```

```yaml
- copy:
    dest: /etc/app/app.conf
    content:
      template: 'port=<%= vars.port %>'
```

```yaml
- copy:
    dest: /etc/sudoers.d/app
    content: 'app ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL'
    validate: 'visudo -cf %s'
```


> ≠ Ansible `copy`: `force` defaults to FALSE here (Ansible defaults TRUE), so copy only rewrites when the destination differs unless you pass force:true. Templating is on-host: pass `content` as an object with `template`/`template_file` and optional `engine` (EJS default, or `jinja`); a bare `content` string is written literally (never interpreted as a template). Attribute application relies on stat/chown/chgrp availability; no SELinux context handling.

## cron

Manage a crontab entry (Ansible `cron` alternate). Entries are marked with `#Ansible: &lt;name&gt;` so present/absent/disabled reconciliation is idempotent and never touches unrelated lines.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Unique entry name (the `#Ansible: &lt;name&gt;` marker). |
| `job` | `string` | optional | Command to run (required when state=present). |
| `minute` | `string` | optional | Cron minute field (default *). |
| `hour` | `string` | optional | Cron hour field (default *). |
| `day` | `string` | optional | Cron day-of-month field (default *). |
| `month` | `string` | optional | Cron month field (default *). |
| `weekday` | `string` | optional | Cron day-of-week field (default *). |
| `special_time` | `string` | optional | Preset schedule (@reboot/@yearly/@annually/@monthly/@weekly/@daily/@hourly). |
| `user` | `string` | optional | Crontab owner (default root). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | optional | Comment the entry out instead of removing it. |
| `cron_file` | `string` | optional | Manage /etc/cron.d/&lt;cron_file&gt; instead of a user crontab. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- cron:
    name: backup-db
    job: /usr/local/bin/backup.sh
    minute: "0"
    hour: "2"
    user: root
```

```yaml
- cron:
    name: nightly-report
    job:
      $concat:
        - /usr/local/bin/report --out /var/log/
        - $var: vars.report_name
    special_time: daily
    cron_file: rolecall-reports
    user: root
```


> ≠ Ansible `cron`: no `backup` (no timestamped crontab backup), no `env`/`insertafter`/`insertbefore`, and no `mode` for a created `cron_file`; `cron_file` accepts an absolute path or a bare name rooted at /etc/cron.d. Uses `$var` refs, not Jinja `{{ }}`.

## fetch

Pull a file from the target to the local control node (Ansible `fetch` alternate). Reads the remote file base64-encoded and skips when the local copy already matches.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | required | Remote path to fetch. |
| `dest` | `string` | required | Local directory to write into. |
| `flat` | `boolean` | optional | Use the bare filename instead of the full path as the local name. |
| `fail_on_missing` | `boolean` | optional | Fail if the remote file is absent (default true). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- fetch:
    src: /var/log/app.log
    dest: /tmp/logs
    flat: true
```


> RoleCall `copy` only pushes; `fetch` is the pull direction (Ansible `fetch`). Local path layout mirrors Ansible: full path with `/` → `_` unless `flat: true`.

## file

Idempotently create/remove directories, files, symlinks, and apply mode/owner/group.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Target path on the host. |
| `state` | `directory \| file \| touch \| link \| absent` | required | Desired state of the path. |
| `mode` | `string` | optional | Octal mode to apply, e.g. '0755'. |
| `owner` | `string` | optional | Owner user to apply. |
| `group` | `string` | optional | Group to apply. |
| `src` | `string` | optional | Link source; required when state is 'link'. |
| `recurse` | `boolean` | optional | Recurse into directories when applying attributes or removing. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- file:
    path:
      $var: vars.web_root
    state: directory
    mode: '0755'
```

```yaml
- file:
    path: /etc/nginx/conf.d/site.conf
    state: touch
    mode: '0644'
```


> ≠ Ansible `file`: naïve shell implementation using `[ -d ]`/`[ -f ]`/`ln -sfn`/`rm`. No SELinux contexts, ACLs, follow/force semantics for links, backup handling, or remote-user validation. mtime is intentionally NOT updated on existing paths during `touch` (kept strictly idempotent).

## find

Search the target filesystem for files/directories (Ansible `find` alternate). Returns matching paths in `data.files`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `paths` | `string \| string[]` | optional | Root path(s) to search (default /). |
| `pattern` | `string` | optional | Name (or regex with `use_regex`) pattern. |
| `file_type` | `file \| directory \| any` | optional | Filter by type (default any). |
| `recurse` | `boolean` | optional | Descend into subdirectories (default true). |
| `depth` | `number` | optional | Max search depth. |
| `use_regex` | `boolean` | optional | Treat `pattern` as a regex. |
| `hidden` | `boolean` | optional | Include dotfiles (default false). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- find:
    paths: /etc
    pattern: "*.conf"
    recurse: true
```


> ≠ Ansible `find`: returns a list of dicts ({path,size,mtime,type,mode}) rather than full `stat`. GNU `find -printf` required. No `size`/`age`/`contains` filters yet.

## git

Clone a repository, or update a local checkout via stash/pull/reset/checkout. Idempotent by comparing current and desired HEAD. Supports shallow clone (depth), forced clean (force), and automatic host-key acceptance (accept_hostkey).

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `repo` | `string` | required | Source repository URL. |
| `dest` | `string` | required | Destination directory. |
| `version` | `string` | optional | Branch/tag/commit to check out (after fetch). |
| `update` | `boolean` | optional | Fetch before checkout (default true). |
| `pull` | `boolean` | optional | Run `git pull` (fetch + merge) to update the current branch. |
| `stash` | `boolean` | optional | Stash local modifications before pull/checkout/reset when the tree is dirty. |
| `reset` | `boolean \| string` | optional | Reset --hard to HEAD (true) or to a ref (string), discarding working-tree changes. |
| `bare` | `boolean` | optional | Clone as a bare repository. |
| `depth` | `number` | optional | Shallow clone depth (commits); passed as `--depth N` to clone and fetch. |
| `force` | `boolean` | optional | Discard local changes (git clean -ffdx + reset --hard to HEAD) before checkout/pull. |
| `accept_hostkey` | `boolean` | optional | Accept the remote SSH host key automatically (StrictHostKeyChecking=no). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- git:
    repo: https://github.com/org/repo
    dest: /opt/repo
    version: main
```

```yaml
- git:
    repo: https://github.com/org/repo
    dest: /opt/repo
    pull: true
    stash: true
```

```yaml
- git:
    repo: https://github.com/org/repo
    dest: /opt/repo
    reset: HEAD
```


> ≠ Ansible `git`: local-tracking refs only (remote refs resolve after `fetch --all`); `pull` is a plain `git pull` (fetch + merge), not rebase. `reset: true` resets --hard to the current HEAD (discards uncommitted work); pair with `stash: true` to shelve first.

## group

Ensure or remove a local/unix group idempotently (present/absent), reconciling GID.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |

```yaml
    state: absent
```


> ≠ Ansible `group`: imperative getent-based implementation using groupadd/groupmod/groupdel over Local/Ssh. No WinNT/AD group backends; GID drift is reconciled with groupmod only when a numeric gid is supplied.

## group_info

Look up a group's gid/members (Ansible `group_info` alternate). Returns `data.group_info`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Group name to look up. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- group_info:

```

## hostname

Set the target hostname (Ansible `hostname` alternate). Uses `hostnamectl set-hostname` on systemd, else writes /etc/hostname.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Desired hostname. |


## http

Idempotent HTTP/REST module: probes current state via GET (or check_url) and converges only when the desired state is absent.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url` | `string` | required | Target URL. |
| `method` | `string` | optional | HTTP method (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS). Default GET. |
| `headers` | `Record&lt;string, string&gt;` | optional | Request headers. |
| `body` | `unknown` | optional | Request body (string verbatim, or JSON when json/non-string). |
| `json` | `boolean` | optional | Serialize body as JSON when true or body is non-string. |
| `expected_status` | `number \| number[]` | optional | Acceptable status code(s); default any 2xx. |
| `check_url` | `string` | optional | URL used by describe to probe state (defaults to url). |
| `state_present` | `boolean` | optional | Expect resource present (true) or absent (false). |
| `match` | `unknown` | optional | Substring or JSON value the probed body must match to be in-desired. |
| `timeout_seconds` | `number` | optional | Per-request hard timeout in seconds. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- http:
    url: https://api.example.com/items/42
    method: PUT
    state_present: true
    headers:
      Authorization:
        $concat:
          - 'Bearer '
          - $var: vars.api_token
    body:
      name: widget
      region:
        $var: vars.site_region
    json: true
```

```yaml
- http:
    url: https://api.example.com/deploy
    method: POST
    body:
      event: deploy
      wait_for_healthy:
        $if:
          then: true
          else: false
          condition:
            $eq:
              - $var: vars.health
              - ready
    json: true
```

```yaml
- http:
    url: https://api.example.com/items/42
    method: DELETE
    state_present: false
```


> ≠ Ansible `uri`: `describe` probes current state with a safe GET (or `check_url`) and only converges when the desired state is absent, so PUT/POST/PATCH are idempotent by default. There is no `status_code`/`return_content` nesting — use `match` + `expected_status`. Safe methods (GET/HEAD/OPTIONS) never report changed.

## iptables

Manage an iptables rule (Ansible `iptables` alternate). Checks via -C, adds via -A/-I, removes via -D.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| `destination_port` | `string` | optional | Destination port. |
| `jump` | `string` | optional | Target, e.g. ACCEPT/DROP (default ACCEPT). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | present (default). |

**Examples**

```yaml
    chain: INPUT
    protocol: tcp
    destination_port: "8080"
    jump: ACCEPT
```

## json_query

Resolve a JSON-pointer (/a/b/0 or $.a.b[0]) path against `data` (Ansible `json_query` alternate). Result in `data.json_query`.

_source: builtin_

## known_hosts

Manage an SSH known_hosts entry (Ansible `known_hosts` alternate). Adds/removes a `name key` line idempotently; defaults to the system /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Hostname or address to trust. |
| `key` | `string` | optional | Public key line (required when state=present). |
| `path` | `string` | optional | known_hosts file (default /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |

**Examples**


## lineinfile

Idempotent line-in-file module: ensures a line is present/absent, replacing a regexp-matched line when given. Supports optional backup and a validate command run on the file after writing.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Destination path on the target. |
| `line` | `string` | optional | Desired line content (required for present state). |
| `regexp` | `string` | optional | Optional regexp matching an existing line to replace. |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |
| `insertafter` | `EOF \| START` | optional | Insert location when absent (default EOF). |
| `backup` | `boolean` | optional | Back up the existing file (a timestamped `.bak` sibling, attributes preserved) before writing. Defaults to false. |
| `validate` | `string` | optional | Validation command run against the file after writing; `%s` is replaced with the file path. The task fails if the command exits non-zero (e.g. `nginx -t -c %s`). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- lineinfile:
    path: /etc/resolv.conf
    regexp: '^nameserver\s+'
    line:
      $concat:
        - 'nameserver '
        - $var: vars.resolver_ip
    state: present
```


> ≠ Ansible `lineinfile`: `insertafter` accepts `EOF` or `START` only (no arbitrary regex anchor yet). Uses `$var` refs, not Jinja `{{ }}`.

Enable or disable a locale (Ansible `locale_gen` alternate). Uncomments the entry in /etc/locale.gen and runs `locale-gen`.

_source: builtin_


## lvg

Create or remove an LVM volume group (Ansible `lvg` alternate). Uses `vgcreate`/`vgremove`; `force` enables `vgremove -f` / `vgcreate --force`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vg` | `string` | required | Volume group name. |
| `pvs` | `string \| string[]` | optional | Physical volumes (required to create). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | present (default). |
| `force` | `boolean` | optional | Force the operation: `vgremove -f` on removal and `vgcreate --force` on creation. Defaults to true for removal (matching prior behaviour); set false to require a clean volume group. |

**Examples**


## lvol

Create or remove an LVM logical volume (Ansible `lvol` alternate). Uses `lvcreate`/`lvremove`.

## meta

Request an executor control action (Ansible `meta` alternate): end_play/end_host/reset_connection/etc.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `end_host` | `boolean` | optional | End for this host. |
| `reset_connection` | `boolean` | optional | Reset the connection. |

| `refresh_inventory` | `boolean` | optional | Refresh inventory. |

**Examples**

```yaml

    end_play: true
```


> `noop`, `reset_connection`, and `clear_facts` act immediately. `end_play` halts the play and `end_host` halts the current host (the executor honors the emitted halt signal). `end_batch`/`refresh_inventory`/`flush_handlers` are surfaced in `data.meta.deferred` for the executor to consume (engine support pending).

Load or unload a kernel module (Ansible `modprobe` alternate). Loads via `modprobe`; persists to /etc/modules-load.d/rolecall-&lt;name&gt;.conf.

Mount or unmount a filesystem (Ansible `mount` alternate). Uses `mount`/`umount`; optionally persists to /etc/fstab.

## openssl_certificate

Declarative X.509 certificate management via openssl: self-signed leaf/CA certs, CA-signed certs, SANs, and per-purpose EKU (server/client/code-signing). Idempotent.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Destination certificate path (PEM). |
| `privatekey_path` | `string` | required | Destination private key path (PEM, unencrypted). |
| `state` | `'present' \| 'absent'` | optional | Default 'present'. 'absent' removes the cert and key. |
| `common_name` | `string` | optional | Certificate CN. |
| `subject` | `string` | optional | Full subject (e.g. '/CN=foo/O=bar'); overrides common_name. |
| `san` | `string[]` | optional | SAN tokens: ['DNS:foo','IP:1.2.3.4','email:a@b']. |
| `days` | `number` | optional | Validity in days (default 365). |
| `algorithm` | `'rsa' \| 'ecdsa' \| 'ed25519'` | optional | Key algorithm (default rsa). |
| `key_size` | `number` | optional | RSA key size (default 2048). |
| `curve` | `string` | optional | Curve (ecdsa) or key type (ed25519). |
| `purpose` | `string \| string[]` | optional | server\|client\|codesign\|email\|timestamp -&gt; EKU. |
| `key_usage` | `string[]` | optional | Explicit keyUsage values. |
| `extended_key_usage` | `string[]` | optional | Explicit extendedKeyUsage values. |
| `ca` | `boolean` | optional | Mint a self-signed CA (basicConstraints=CA:TRUE). |
| `ca_cert` | `string` | optional | CA cert to sign with (enables CA-signed mode). |
| `ca_key` | `string` | optional | CA private key (with ca_cert). |
| `csr` | `string` | optional | Existing CSR to sign (CA mode only). |
| `force` | `boolean` | optional | Regenerate even if an existing cert matches. |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | optional | Plan only; execute nothing. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- openssl_certificate:
    path: /etc/nginx/ssl/site.crt
    privatekey_path: /etc/nginx/ssl/site.key
    common_name: site1.example.com
    san:
      - 'DNS:site1.example.com'
    purpose: server
```

```yaml
- openssl_certificate:
    path: /etc/ca/ca.crt
    privatekey_path: /etc/ca/ca.key
    common_name: My Internal CA
    ca: true
```

```yaml
- openssl_certificate:
    path: /etc/nginx/ssl/client.crt
    privatekey_path: /etc/nginx/ssl/client.key
    common_name: admin
    purpose: client
    ca_cert: /etc/ca/ca.crt
    ca_key: /etc/ca/ca.key
```


> ≠ Ansible `community.crypto.openssl_certificate`: covers self-signed, CA, and CA-signed certs with SANs + EKU. Idempotent via on-target inspection (subject/SAN/expiry). Requires the `openssl` CLI on the target.

## package

Detects the target package manager (apt/dnf/yum/apk/pacman/zypper) and installs/removes a package idempotently.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Package name, e.g. 'nginx'. |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default 'present'). |
| `version` | `string` | optional | Pin an exact version using native PM syntax at install time. |
| `update_cache` | `boolean` | optional | For apt: run `apt-get update` before installing (default false). |
| `cache_valid_time` | `number` | optional | For apt: treat as update_cache when &gt; 0 (cache-age check is not yet implemented). |
| `src` | `string` | optional | Local package file (.deb/.rpm/.apk) to install instead of a repo name. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- package:
    name: nginx
    state: present
```

```yaml
- package:
    name: nginx
    version: 1.26.0-1~bookworm
    state: absent
```

```yaml
- package:
    name: nginx
    src: /tmp/nginx_1.26.0-1~bookworm_amd64.deb
```


> ≠ Ansible `package`/`apt`/`dnf`/`yum`: auto-detects one of apt/dnf/yum/apk/pacman/zypper (first match wins); no per-task `manager` override. Version syntax maps to each PM's native form. `src` installs a local file. No `hold`, `allow_downgrade`, or transactional rollback yet.

## pam_limits

Manage an /etc/security/limits.conf entry (Ansible `pam_limits` alternate). Adds/removes a `domain type item value` line.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `domain` | `string` | required | Limit domain (user/group/*). |
| `type` | `soft \| hard \| -` | required | Limit type. |
| `item` | `string` | required | Limit item (e.g. nofile). |
| `value` | `string` | required | Limit value. |
| `dest` | `string` | optional | limits.conf path (default /etc/security/limits.conf). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | present (default). |
| `use_first_match` | `boolean` | optional | When present and an exact match is absent, replace the first line beginning with `domain type item ` rather than appending a new line. |

**Examples**

```yaml

    domain: "*"
    type: soft
    item: nofile
    value: "65536"
```

## parted

Create or remove a partition with parted (Ansible `parted` alternate). Creates the label if missing, then mkpart + flags.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

## replace

Replace text in a file (literal old→replace or regexp→replace), writing back only when content changes. Idempotent. Supports optional backup and a validate command run on the temp file before it is moved into place.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Target file path. |
| `old` | `string` | optional | Literal string to replace. |
| `regexp` | `string` | optional | Regular expression (global) to replace. |
| `replace` | `string` | required | Replacement text. |
| `backup` | `boolean` | optional | Rotate a timestamped .bak before writing. |
| `validate` | `string` | optional | Validation command run against the temp file before it is moved into place; `%s` is replaced with the temp path. The task fails if the command exits non-zero (e.g. `nginx -t -c %s`). |

## script

Ansible `script` alias of `shell`. Reads a local `src` script (control node) and runs it on the target via `shell`. Defaults `run_mode: always`, or `idempotent` with a `creates`/`removes` guard.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | required | Local path to the script on the control node. |
| `creates` | `string` | optional | Skip when this path exists (maps to shell idempotent guard). |
| `removes` | `string` | optional | Skip when this path is absent (maps to shell idempotent guard). |
| `run_mode` | `idempotent \| readonly \| always` | optional | Override the forwarded shell run_mode (default: always, or idempotent with a guard). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- script:
    src: roles/web/files/setup.sh
```


> ≠ Ansible `script`: `script` is an alias of `shell` — it sets `local_src` to your `src` and forwards to `shell`. You can use `shell` directly with `local_src` instead. Guards (`creates`/`removes`) make it `run_mode: idempotent`; otherwise it is `run_mode: always`.

Set SELinux enforcing/permissive/disabled or toggle a boolean (Ansible `selinux`/`seboolean` alternate).

| `state` | `enforcing \| permissive \| disabled` | optional | SELinux mode to set. |
| `boolean` | `string` | optional | SELinux boolean name to toggle. |
| `value` | `on \| off` | optional | Boolean value (with boolean). |

## service

Idempotent service enable/start/stop (Ansible `service`/`systemd` alternate). Probes current state before acting; supports `daemon_reload`, `state: reloaded`, and a SysV `service` fallback when systemd is absent.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Unit name, e.g. 'nginx'. |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | optional | Enable the unit (default true). |
| `state` | `started \| stopped \| restarted \| reloaded` | optional | Desired active state (default 'started'). |
| `daemon_reload` | `boolean` | optional | Run `systemctl daemon-reload` first (systemd only). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- service:
    name:
      $var: vars.pkg_name
    enabled: true
    state: started
```

```yaml
- service:
    name: nginx
    state: reloaded
    daemon_reload: true
```


> ≠ Ansible `service`/`systemd`: `pattern`/`sleep`/`scope`/`runlevel` are accepted but currently no-ops. SysV fallback uses the `service` init script when `systemctl` is missing; no `daemon_reload` under SysV.

Gather service units on systemd targets (Ansible `service_facts` alternate). Returns `data.services` keyed by unit name with {enabled, state}.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

_(none)_

**Examples**

```yaml

```


> ≠ Ansible `service_facts`: systemd-only. `state` is the active state from `systemctl list-units` (running/exited/dead/…); `enabled` from `list-unit-files`. SysV/Upstart not enumerated.

## set_fact

Assign host variables from the task args (Ansible `set_fact` alternate). Each key is persisted live to the host's fact map and is readable downstream via `$var: facts.&lt;key&gt;`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*` | `any` | optional | Arbitrary key/value pairs become facts. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- set_fact:
    foo: bar
- debug:
    msg:
      $var: facts.foo
```


> Like Ansible `set_fact`, each key is persisted live to the host's fact map and is visible to downstream tasks via `$var: facts.foo` (e.g. `{$var: "facts.foo"}`). Reserve this for values that are genuinely a persistent fact about the host; use `set_reg` for runtime scratch variables.

## set_reg

Assign runtime register values from the task args. Each key is persisted live to the run's `reg` store and is readable downstream via `$var: reg.&lt;key&gt;`. Use for runtime scratch variables (cached tokens, computed intermediates), not host facts.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*` | `any` | optional | Arbitrary key/value pairs become register values (read via `$var: reg.*`). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- set_reg:
    deploy_token: abc123
- debug:
    msg:
      $var: reg.deploy_token
```


> Each key is persisted live to the run's `reg` store and is visible to downstream tasks via `$var: reg.foo` (e.g. `{$var: "reg.foo"}`). Unlike `set_fact`, these are runtime variables (not host facts). Prefer `set_reg` for runtime scratch values and reserve `set_fact` for genuine persistent host facts.

## set_stats

Surface run stats (Ansible `set_stats` alternate). Returns `data.set_stats`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `data` | `object` | required | Stats payload to surface. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- set_stats:
    data:
      deployed: true
```


> Each key of `data` is aggregated into the run-level stat store (objects deep-merge, scalars overwrite) and persists for the life of the run; the payload is also returned in `data.set_stats`.

## shell

Idempotency-aware CLI module controlled by `run_mode` (idempotent\|readonly\|always; default idempotent). In `idempotent` mode a guard (creates/removes/creates_cmd/removes_cmd) is required or apply throws; `readonly` runs every time but reports changed:false (a pure check); `always` runs every time and is always changed. Supports --dry-run, verify_cmd, a per-task timeout_seconds (seconds), and an explicit executable (shell binary).

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | `string` | required | Command to run (alias: cmd). Use the $template operator to embed vars/facts. |
| `cmd` | `string` | optional | Alias for command. |
| `src` | `string` | optional | Path to a script/file already on the target; run it directly (alternative to `command`). |
| `local_src` | `string` | optional | Path to a script on the control node; read here and execute via the target shell (the `script` module is an alias of this). |
| `run_mode` | `string` | optional | How the task treats idempotency. `idempotent` (default): require a guard or apply throws; `readonly`: run every time but always report changed:false (a pure check); `always`: run every time and always report changed:true. See Writing idempotent shell tasks (/concepts/shell-idempotency). |
| `creates` | `string` | optional | When this path exists on the target, the task is already done (skip). |
| `removes` | `string` | optional | When this path is absent on the target, the task is already done (skip). |
| `creates_cmd` | `string` | optional | Precedence guard: full shell command; if it exits 0 the work is already done (skip). Takes precedence over creates/removes. |
| `removes_cmd` | `string` | optional | Precedence guard: full shell command; if it exits non-zero the work is already done (skip). Takes precedence over creates/removes. |
| `verify_cmd` | `string` | optional | Post-check: after the main command runs, exec it; exitCode !== 0 marks the result failed (changed is otherwise unchanged). |
| `dry_run` | `boolean` | optional | Dry-run: report what would run, execute nothing. |
| `timeout_seconds` | `number` | optional | Optional per-task exec timeout in seconds (long-running commands only; the transport default applies otherwise). |
| `executable` | `string` | optional | Explicit shell/process binary used to run the command (e.g. /bin/bash); defaults to /bin/sh (local) or the remote login shell. The command is executed as `&lt;executable&gt; -c '&lt;cmd&gt;'`. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- shell:
    command: systemctl restart nginx
    creates: /run/nginx.pid
```

```yaml
- shell:
    command: enable-feature --apply
    creates_cmd: feature --status | grep -q enabled
    verify_cmd: curl -sf http://localhost/health
```

```yaml
# One-shot / fire-and-forget? Run every time, always changed:
- shell:
    command: "apt-get install -y nginx"
    run_mode: always
```

```yaml
# Pure read-only check (runs every time, never "changed"):
- shell:
    command: "nginx -t"
    run_mode: readonly
```

```yaml
# Reference vars/facts with $template (RoleCall does not render {{ }}):
- shell:
    command:
      $template: "echo host <%= vars.cimc_host %> is <%= facts.os %>"
    run_mode: always
```

```yaml
# Multi-line scripts pass verbatim to /bin/sh (newlines preserved):
- shell:
    command: |
      set -e
      echo "bootstrapping <%= vars.role %>"
      touch /opt/app/.bootstrapped
    run_mode: always
```

```yaml
# Long-running commands: set a timeout in seconds (the transport default applies otherwise):
- shell:
    command: "make -C /src all"
    run_mode: always
    timeout_seconds: 1800
```

```yaml
# Run via an explicit shell/process instead of /bin/sh:
- shell:
    command: "source /opt/venv/bin/activate && pip list"
    executable: /bin/bash
    run_mode: always
```


> ≠ Ansible `shell`: executes via `/bin/sh` (local) or the remote login shell over SSH unless an explicit `executable` is set (then `&lt;executable&gt; -c '&lt;cmd&gt;'`) — RoleCall has no `command` vs `shell` split. Guarded by default via `run_mode: idempotent` (set `run_mode: always` for unguarded runs, `run_mode: readonly` for pure checks). When idempotent, skips via creates/removes/creates_cmd/removes_cmd so re-runs can be no-ops. The command comes from `command`/`cmd` (inline), `local_src` (a control-node script read here — the `script` module is an alias of this), or `src` (a script already on the target, run directly). A guard combined with `run_mode: readonly`/`always` throws. See Writing idempotent shell tasks (/concepts/shell-idempotency) for the full guide, including multi-line scripts, $template vars/facts, and read-only checks.

## slurp

Read a remote file's contents into a variable (Ansible `slurp` alternate). Returns decoded text and base64 in `data.slurp`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | required | Remote path to read. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- slurp:
    src: /etc/hostname
  register: hn
```


> ≠ Ansible `slurp`: the decoded text lives at `register.data.slurp.content` (Ansible nests it under `content` directly).

## sql

Idempotent SQL module: runs the mutating query only when check_query shows the desired state is not yet present.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `db` | `string` | required | Path to the SQLite database file (created if missing). |
| `query` | `string` | required | Mutating SQL statement to run on converge (idempotent via check_query). |
| `check_query` | `string` | optional | Probe: when it returns &gt;= expected_rows rows, state is in-desired. |
| `params` | `unknown[]` | optional | Bound parameters for query. |
| `check_params` | `unknown[]` | optional | Bound parameters for check_query. |
| `expected_rows` | `number` | optional | Rows check_query must return to be considered applied (default 1). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- sql:
    db: app.db
    query: 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users(id INTEGER)'
    check_query: "SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table' AND name='users'"
    expected_rows: 1
```

```yaml
- sql:
    db:
      $var: vars.db_path
    query:
      $call: migrate_users
    check_query: "SELECT max(version) FROM schema_migrations"
    params:
      - $var: vars.target_version
```

## stat

Read-only: report whether a target path exists and its kind/attributes.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | required | Path on the target to inspect. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- stat:
    path: /etc/nginx/nginx.conf
  register: conf_stat
```

```yaml
- stat:
    path:
      $var: vars.web_root
  loop:
    $var: vars.paths_to_check
```


> ≠ Ansible `stat`: read-only probe implemented with POSIX `[ -e/-d/-f/-L ]` tests plus GNU `stat -c`; there is no `follow` toggle (always resolves symlinks), no `checksum`/`md5sum` side effect, no `get_checksum`, and `islnk` reflects whether the entry itself is a symlink while `isdir`/`isfile` describe the resolved target. `mtime` is emitted as an ISO-8601 string rather than Ansible's parsed datetime object.

## synchronize

rsync files on the target (Ansible `synchronize` alternate). NOTE: runs rsync on the target itself, not controller→target.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | required | Source path (on target). |
| `dest` | `string` | required | Destination path (on target). |
| `delete` | `boolean` | optional | Mirror deletions (--delete). |
| `recursive` | `boolean` | optional | Use -a (default true). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- synchronize:
    src: /srv/www/
    dest: /var/www/
    delete: true
```


> ≠ Ansible `synchronize`: Ansible runs rsync from the controller to the target; RoleCall runs rsync on the target (src/dest are both on the target). No `mode: pull` controller semantics.

## sysctl

Set a kernel parameter (Ansible `sysctl` alternate). Reads /proc/sys, applies via `sysctl -w`, persists to /etc/sysctl.d/99-rolecall.conf.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Parameter name, e.g. net.ipv4.ip_forward. |
| `value` | `string` | optional | Value to set (required when state=present). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | present (default) or absent. |
| `sysctl_file` | `string` | optional | Persisted-file path for the setting (default /etc/sysctl.d/99-rolecall.conf). |
| `ignoreerrors` | `boolean` | optional | Continue (do not fail the task) when `sysctl` returns a non-zero exit. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- sysctl:
    name: net.ipv4.ip_forward
    value: "1"
```


> ≠ Ansible `sysctl`: persists to a single default file (override with `sysctl_file`); `ignoreerrors` continues past non-zero `sysctl` exits.

## tempfile

Create a temp file or directory on the target (Ansible `tempfile` alternate). Returns the path in `data.path`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | `string` | optional | Directory to create in (default /tmp). |
| `prefix` | `string` | optional | Filename prefix. |
| `suffix` | `string` | optional | Filename suffix. |
| `state` | `file \| directory` | optional | Create a file or directory (default file). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- tempfile:
    path: /tmp
    prefix: app-
    state: directory
  register: tmp
```


> ≠ Ansible `tempfile`: always creates a new node (`changed: true`); RoleCall does not yet track/clean it up automatically.

## timezone

Set the system timezone (Ansible `timezone` alternate). Uses `timedatectl set-timezone` when available.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Timezone, e.g. UTC or Europe/London. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- timezone:
    name: UTC
```


> ≠ Ansible `timezone`: no `hwclock` sync toggle; only sets the OS timezone.

## ufw

Manage UFW firewall rules and enable/disable (Ansible `ufw` alternate).

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rule` | `allow \| deny \| limit \| reject` | optional | Action (default allow). |
| `port` | `string` | optional | Port or port range. |
| `proto` | `tcp \| udp` | optional | Protocol. |
| `state` | `enabled \| disabled` | optional | Enable/disable the firewall. |
| `direction` | `in \| out` | optional | Rule direction. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- ufw:
    rule: allow
    port: "22"
    proto: tcp
```

```yaml
- ufw:
    state: enabled
```


> ≠ Ansible `ufw`: `ufw allow` is naturally idempotent on the host; no `default` policy arg (set via a `shell` task).

## unarchive

Extract an archive on the target (Ansible `unarchive` alternate). Supports .tar/.tar.gz/.tgz/.zip; skips when `creates` exists.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src` | `string` | required | Remote archive path to extract. |
| `dest` | `string` | required | Remote directory to extract into. |
| `creates` | `string` | optional | Skip the task if this path exists. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- unarchive:
    src: /tmp/app.tar.gz
    dest: /opt/app
    creates: /opt/app/.installed
```


> ≠ Ansible `unarchive`: `remote_src` is always true (RoleCall extracts on the target); no `keep_newer`/per-file diff — re-running re-extracts unless `creates` guards it.

## user

Ensure or remove a local/unix account idempotently (present/absent), reconciling uid/gid/home/shell/groups.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Account/login name. Required. |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default 'present'). |
| `uid` | `number` | optional | Numeric UID to enforce at creation/reconcile. |
| `gid` | `number` | optional | Numeric GID to enforce (also sets primary group). |
| `group` | `string` | optional | Group name resolved into a GID (alternative to gid). |
| `home` | `string` | optional | Login/home directory path. |
| `shell` | `string` | optional | Login shell path. |
| `create_home` | `boolean` | optional | Create the home directory at creation time (default true unless explicitly false). |
| `groups` | `string` | optional | Comma-separated supplementary groups. Use append to merge instead of replace. |
| `append` | `boolean` | optional | Append groups to the existing set instead of replacing it. |
| `system` | `boolean` | optional | Create a system account. |
| `password` | `string` | optional | Cleartext password applied via chpasswd when provided. |
| `remove` | `boolean` | optional | Delete home dir + mail spool on removal (userdel -r). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- user:
    name: alice
    state: present
    uid: 1050
    shell: /usr/bin/fish
```

```yaml
- user:
    name: deploy
    state: absent
    remove: true
```


> ≠ Ansible `user`: imperative getent-based implementation using useradd/usermod/userdel/chpasswd over Local/Ssh. Passwords are sent in cleartext via chpasswd (no hashing); no login-history validation, no encrypted-password (`password_hash`) support, and no OpenSSH/LDAP account backends.

## user_info

Look up a user's uid/gid/home/shell/groups (Ansible `user_info` alternate). Returns `data.user_info`.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | User name to look up. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- user_info:
    name: deploy
```


> ≠ Ansible `user_info`: relies on getent/id (POSIX); no `forks`/parallel gather. Mirrors the `user` module's read side.

## wait_for

Poll until a TCP port is open or a path exists (Ansible `wait_for` alternate). Reports `changed: false` once satisfied; fails after `timeout` seconds.

_source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `port` | `number` | optional | TCP port to probe (with `host`). |
| `host` | `string` | optional | Host to probe (default 127.0.0.1). |
| `path` | `string` | optional | Filesystem path that must exist. |
| `timeout` | `number` | optional | Seconds to wait (default 300). |
| `delay` | `number` | optional | Seconds to wait before first probe. |

**Examples**

```yaml
- wait_for:
    port: 8000
    host: "{{ vars.app_host }}"
    timeout: 60
```

```yaml
- wait_for:
    path: /var/run/app.sock
    timeout: 30
```


> ≠ Ansible `wait_for`: only `port`/`path` polling is implemented (no `search_regex` on socket output, no `active_connection` states). Port probing uses bash `/dev/tcp`.

## yum_repository

Manage a YUM/DNF repo file section (Ansible `yum_repository` alternate). Writes an `[&lt;name&gt;]` INI section to /etc/yum.repos.d/&lt;file&gt;.repo idempotently and preserves other sections.

_idempotent · source: builtin_

**Args**

| Arg | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | required | Repo id (the `[&lt;name&gt;]` section). |
| `description` | `string` | optional | Human-readable repository name (defaults to the repo id). |
| `baseurl` | `string` | optional | Base URL. |
| `mirrorlist` | `string` | optional | Mirrorlist URL. |
| `metalink` | `string` | optional | Metalink URL. |
| `gpgcheck` | `boolean` | optional | Enable GPG signature check (default false). |
| `repo_gpgcheck` | `boolean` | optional | Enable GPG check of metadata (written only when set). |
| `enabled` | `boolean` | optional | Enable the repo (default true). |
| `gpgkey` | `string` | optional | GPG key URL used to verify packages. |
| `file` | `string` | optional | Repo filename without extension (default = name). |
| `state` | `present \| absent` | optional | Desired state (default present). |

**Examples**

```yaml
- yum_repository:
    name: nginx-stable
    description: nginx stable
    baseurl: http://nginx.org/packages/centos/7/$basearch/
    gpgcheck: false
    enabled: true
```

```yaml
- yum_repository:
    name: epel
    description: Extra Packages for Enterprise Linux
    mirrorlist: https://mirrors.fedoraproject.org/metalink?repo=epel-9&arch=$basearch
    gpgcheck: true
    gpgkey: https://dl.fedoraproject.org/pub/epel/RPM-GPG-KEY-EPEL-9
```


> ≠ Ansible `yum_repository`: only the base INI fields are written (no `cost`/`priority`/`exclude`/`includepkgs`/`sslcacert`/`sslverify`, no `gpgkey` auto-import — add a `shell` task to import keys). `description` defaults to the repo id, `enabled` to true, and `gpgcheck` to false. Uses `$var` refs, not Jinja `{{ }}`.
